papers.title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.
papers.summary: This analysis of the STS/ACC TVT Registry asked whether early-career TAVR operators, defined as 5 years or less in independent practice, achieve outcomes comparable to more experienced peers. It included 634,723 isolated TAVR procedures performed between October 2011 and March 2024 by 3,126 operators at 847 US sites; 90,376 procedures (14.2%) were done by early-career operators. Hierarchical models adjusted for patient, procedural, operator and site factors, including institutional TAVR volume. Early-career operators performed fewer cases, with a median annualised lifetime volume of 13 versus 19 per year. After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.01). The 30-day composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was modestly lower with early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.93 to 0.98). The authors conclude that early-career status alone should not be a barrier to independent practice.
papers.critique: Best: an enormous national registry spanning thirteen years, hierarchical models that account for clustering and adjust for institutional volume, and a practical workforce question. Weakest: it is observational, so residual confounding is likely. Early-career operators usually work within established heart teams, often alongside senior colleagues, which the registry cannot capture, and case selection may differ. Outcomes stop at 30 days, so valve durability and late events are unknown, and the composite difference of 0.6 percentage points is small. No independent commentary on this paper was found yet; TCTMD's report on a related TVT volume study quoted its lead author, Dharam Kumbhani, cautioning that such analyses show association, not causation.

papers.title: Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes.
papers.short_title: five-year results of transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty
papers.summary: This prospective, multicentre NHLBI early feasibility study reports 5-year follow-up after transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty. The device places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants with a median age of 73 years; 63% were female, 63% had reduced and 37% preserved ejection fraction. Between 1 and 5 years the investigators collected vital status, serious adverse events, clinical records and site-reported echocardiography. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant received an LVAD after 2 years and one underwent mitral TEER after 3 years; none had heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, 4 of whom needed new cardiac devices. Among those with follow-up imaging, mitral regurgitation fell and ejection fraction improved through 5 years, but symptom benefit was greatest in the first year and faded thereafter.
papers.critique: Best: rare five-year data on a novel, implant-light transcatheter approach from an experienced NHLBI team, with candid reporting of a serious safety signal. Weakest: only 18 participants, no control group and incomplete follow-up. The full text notes that after year one echocardiography was site-reported without core laboratory review, medications were not recorded, and symptoms were taken retrospectively from clinic notes rather than validated tools such as KCCQ. Complete heart block in a third of patients, which halted the study, is a major barrier to adoption, and 57% survival cannot be attributed to the device. No independent commentary on this paper was found yet.

papers.title: First and Subsequent Major Cardiovascular Events With Oral Semaglutide in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes: A Secondary Analysis of the SOUL Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.short_title: oral semaglutide and total cardiovascular events in diabetes
papers.summary: This prespecified secondary analysis of the double-blind SOUL trial randomised 9,650 adults with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease or both to once-daily oral semaglutide, up to 14 mg, or placebo, with median follow-up of 49.5 months. Counting first and subsequent events, there were 683 major adverse cardiovascular events with semaglutide versus 791 with placebo (mean ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.76 to 0.97). Discontinuation for adverse events was 15.5% versus 11.6%.
papers.study_type: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial
papers.relevance: A tablet GLP-1 option that reduces the total, not just first, burden of MI, stroke and cardiovascular death in high-risk diabetic patients, many of whom pass through the cath lab.

papers.title: Assessment of Coronary Inflammatory Risk From Noncontrast Cardiac Computed Tomography.
papers.short_title: coronary inflammation on noncontrast CT beyond calcium score
papers.summary: In this multicentre cohort, an artificial intelligence algorithm measured the coronary fat attenuation index, a marker of coronary inflammation, on noncontrast cardiac CT performed for calcium scoring. It was derived in 6,818 people and validated in 19,110, with 536 cardiovascular deaths over a median 6.7 years. The index stratified cardiovascular mortality across calcium score categories, most strongly at a score of zero, and improved discrimination when added to calcium score, raising the area under the curve from 0.76 to 0.80.
papers.relevance: If confirmed prospectively, a routine calcium-score scan could also flag inflamed but calcium-free coronaries in patients now labelled low risk.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
papers.short_title: cardiovascular health promotion for US veterans
papers.summary: This American Heart Association scientific statement applies the Life's Essential 8 framework, extended to mental health and substance use, to US veterans, a population with high cardiovascular risk shaped by military service. It reviews guidelines, barriers and Veterans Affairs programmes such as team-based primary care, MOVE! weight management and telehealth. Veterans in VA care often match or exceed non-VA peers, but gaps remain in lifestyle, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, mental health care and sleep disorders.
papers.relevance: Mainly of US health-system interest, with little direct bearing on interventional practice in Ireland.
